name: IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro)
tagline: Shrinking door: most fresher seats in India, but fewer each year and pay flat since 2008

door_size.caveat: Sum of five companies' own FY26 statements (TCS 44,000 trainees, Infosys 20,000, Cognizant 20,000, HCLTech 11,000, Wipro 7,500), rounded down; the industry took about 4 lakh freshers in FY22 and an estimated 1.6 lakh in FY24, so the door has roughly halved in four years and Wipro has no FY27 target at all.

pay_band.note: TCS and Infosys base offers are around Rs 3.1 to 3.4 lakh and have not moved since about 2008; specialist tracks (Infosys DSE, TCS Digital and Prime, Cognizant GenC Next, Accenture AASE) pay roughly double for a small share who clear a harder coding test.

tiers_realistic.tier1: Yes, but most tier-1 graduates treat these offers as a floor; the specialist tracks (Rs 7 to 9 lakh) are where tier-1 candidates actually join.
tiers_realistic.tier2: Yes; this is the core catchment. Campus drives still visit well-known state and private colleges, though intake per college has fallen and offer-to-joining gaps of 6 to 12 months are common.
tiers_realistic.tier3: Yes, this remains the most realistic first job for a tier-3 graduate, through open tests (TCS NQT, Infosys off-campus, Cognizant GenC, Accenture ASE, Capgemini, Mphasis) rather than campus visits. What substitutes for the brand: a 60%+ academic record with no backlogs, a clear aptitude and basic coding test score, spoken English good enough for a client call, and one small deployed project. Be honest with yourself that seats are fewer each year (five firms' net headcount fell in FY26, demand.top5_it.net_headcount.fy26) and only 35% of IT employers intended to hire freshers in ISR 2026 (supply.isr2026.it_fresher_hiring_intent).

entry_requirements: 60% or 6.0 CGPA throughout (10th, 12th, degree) with no active backlogs; most mass recruiters hard-filter on this
Aptitude plus basic programming test (TCS NQT, Infosys InfyTQ-style, Cognizant GenC, Wipro NLTH, Accenture cognitive and coding assessment): arrays, strings, SQL queries, simple OOP in Java or Python
Spoken and written English at a level that passes a communication round; Accenture and Cognizant test this explicitly
One programming language to working level (Java or Python) plus SQL; for specialist tracks, LeetCode-easy DSA and a second language
Willingness to sign a service agreement and accept any base location and any project (banking, insurance, retail, telecom support are the usual first postings)

Increasingly: a certificate in cloud (AWS or Azure fundamentals) or a GenAI foundations badge; TCS reports 312,000 AI/ML-proficient staff (demand.tcs.ai_ml_proficient.q1fy27) and expects trainees to start at that baseline
Eligibility often limited to the current and previous two batches (2024 to 2026), so apply in the graduation year

two_year_plan.title: Clear the filters: aptitude, one language, SQL
learn: Quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning and verbal ability: free resources (IndiaBIX, PrepInsta free tier, NPTEL 'Aptitude' lectures); 45 minutes a day
Java or Python to the level of writing a 50-line program from a problem statement without help; NPTEL 'Programming in Java' or CS50P
SQL basics through joins and group by on PostgreSQL or MySQL

TCS NQT syllabus and Infosys, Cognizant GenC, Accenture test patterns; register on TCS NextStep, Infosys Careers, Accenture India campus portal, Capgemini Students/Graduates and Mphasis campus pages in your final year
build: A small Java or Python console application (library, billing or attendance) with a MySQL backend, on GitHub
evidence: Timed mock test scores tracked weekly

two_year_plan.title: Aim for the specialist track, not just the base offer
learn: DSA to LeetCode-easy plus some medium (100 problems): this is what separates Infosys DSE, TCS Digital and Prime, Cognizant GenC Next and Accenture AASE from the base offer
A cloud fundamentals certificate: AWS Cloud Practitioner (free training) or Azure AZ-900 via FutureSkills Prime at no cost
Spring Boot (Java) or Django/FastAPI (Python) basics; REST APIs; Git
GenAI foundations: how to call an LLM API, what RAG is, prompt basics; recruiters now ask for this even at base level
build: A REST API with a database and a simple front end, deployed on a free tier, with an LLM-powered feature (for example, a support chatbot over the product's FAQ)
evidence: TCS Digital or Infosys DSE test attempt
target: TCS Digital and Prime via NQT
Cognizant GenC Next and GenC Pro

two_year_plan.title: First posting: become useful fast, pick a domain
learn: Whatever your training batch teaches (usually Java full stack, .NET, SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow or testing): finish the internal certification in the first attempt
The client's domain: banking, insurance, retail or telecom; read the process documents nobody else reads
Agentic tooling used on the account (GitHub Copilot, internal assistants): learn to review AI-generated code and tests, because that review is the job now

If still waiting for a joining date: the same cloud and GenAI material, plus a NATS graduate apprenticeship (Rs 12,300 per month stipend, paths.skilling.nats_graduate_stipend.2026) rather than sitting idle
build: One automation for your own team's repetitive work (a script, a dashboard, a test suite) and show it to your lead
evidence: A written summary of what you automated and time saved
target: Your own account's rotation to a development role

two_year_plan.title: Use the job as a base to move up or across
learn: Choose one exit: (a) a specialist role inside (cloud, data engineering, SAP, cybersecurity) with the vendor certificate (AWS Solutions Architect Associate, Azure Data Engineer, SAP), or (b) the ai_native_software path with a portfolio built on evenings, or (c) a GCC role in the same domain
Interview preparation for GCCs: DSA medium, system design basics, domain questions
build: The evidenced project below, built in the domain of your first posting, outside work hours and with no client data
target: GCCs in your domain (banking or insurance captives)
Specialist tracks in your own company

evidenced_project_spec.title: Order-to-cash reconciliation service for a retail chain
evidenced_project_spec.scope: A service that ingests daily sales files from 20 synthetic stores (POS CSV exports), payment-gateway settlement files and bank statements, matches them, flags mismatches with reasons, exposes a REST API and a small dashboard, and lets a finance user ask questions about exceptions in plain language via an LLM tool that only queries the reconciled tables. Includes automated tests, a nightly scheduled run and a runbook.
evidenced_project_spec.agent_use: A coding agent generates the CSV parsers, test fixtures and the first version of the matching rules; the graduate specifies the matching logic in writing first, reviews every generated function against it, and keeps a changelog of the agent's mistakes (wrong date handling, missed partial settlements). The LLM query feature is built with strict read-only SQL and a small eval set of 30 finance questions.
evidenced_project_spec.done_looks_like: Runs end to end nightly on a free-tier VM; matches 98% of synthetic transactions correctly with every mismatch labelled; the finance chat answers 25 of 30 eval questions correctly and refuses out-of-scope requests; README explains the business process (order, invoice, settlement, bank credit), the rules and the failure cases.
evidenced_project_spec.verification: Test suite in CI with a published coverage number; a seeded set of 50 known mismatches that the system must catch every run; a 30-minute walkthrough the graduate can give covering the retail cash cycle, one rule that was wrong and how it was found, and why the LLM is restricted to read-only queries; a reviewer from finance or a faculty member signs off on five outputs.

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Manual and scripted testing on a fresher bench (the largest fresher intake)
ai_task_shift.now: Agents generate and run regression suites; testing benches are the first seats cut, which is why fresher intake halved between FY22 and FY24
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Test strategy, exploratory testing of business flows, and signing off that the client's process actually works

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Level-1 application support: read the ticket, follow the runbook, escalate
ai_task_shift.now: Agents triage, summarise and resolve routine tickets; TCS says its delivery model, not layoffs, changed and it expects fewer trainees per unit of work
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Level-2 root-cause work, changes that touch the client's data, and talking to the client

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Write CRUD screens and reports to a specification
ai_task_shift.now: Copilots draft the code; the trainee is expected to review, test and integrate, and to know the domain well enough to spot a wrong assumption
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Requirement clarification, domain rules, code review and accountability for production

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Migrate code between versions or platforms by hand (legacy modernisation)
ai_task_shift.now: Agents do bulk translation; large modernisation deals still need people to verify behaviour and fix edge cases
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Verification design, edge-case handling, and cutover planning

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Prepare status reports, documentation and meeting notes
ai_task_shift.now: Generated automatically from tickets and calls
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Deciding what matters, negotiating scope, and client relationships; communication skills now count for more, not less

fit_rules.reason: Accepted everywhere; your competition here is every other branch, so aim for the specialist track.
Mass recruiters take ECE at the same rate as CS if you pass the coding test.
Mass recruiters still take Mechanical and Electrical graduates when core jobs are scarce; the test does not depend on your branch.
This is the path where a tier-3 college matters least: open tests like TCS NQT and Infosys off-campus do not look at your college.
Campus drives still visit tier-2 colleges, though with fewer seats than before.
You will likely get this offer, but treat it as a floor; better doors are open to you.
Most drives accept the previous two batches, so an already-graduated candidate can still apply through 2026.
The 2026 batch is in the eligibility window for every current drive.
Offers come with a base location you do not choose; accepting any city is often the difference between an offer and none.
Mass recruiters post you where the project is; refusing relocation usually means the offer lapses.
This is the fastest route to a salary for most graduates, even though joining dates can slip.
With a year of runway you can afford to aim at a better-paying door first and keep this as fallback.
Day-to-day work is software delivery, mostly maintenance and support at the start.
Client communication and coordination matter more as routine coding is automated.
There is little research or theory in entry-level services work.
The largest number of fresher seats and the shortest time to a first salary.
Intake is falling and five firms' net headcount shrank in FY26; the first job is real but not a long-term guarantee.
Base pay has been about Rs 3 lakh for nearly two decades; growth is slow unless you move to a specialist track or out.
Coding practice lifts you from the base track to the specialist track, which roughly doubles pay.
